name: Silk Road
description: The ancient overland network connecting East Asia to the Mediterranean, facilitating exchange of silk, spices, precious metals, and ideas across civilizations
economic_impact: Largest pre-modern trade network; enabled cultural diffusion of Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity; transmitted technologies like papermaking and gunpowder; generated enormous wealth for intermediary kingdoms

name: Maritime Spice Route
description: Maritime routes connecting South Asia and Southeast Asia to the Spice Islands, carrying cloves, nutmeg, pepper, and cinnamon
economic_impact: Primary motivation for European Age of Exploration; spice monopolies generated extraordinary profits; drove colonial competition between Portugal, Netherlands, and England

name: Trans-Saharan Gold-Salt Trade
description: Caravan routes crossing the Sahara Desert linking North Africa with West Africa, exchanging gold and salt as primary commodities
economic_impact: Created some of the wealthiest empires in medieval world; Mansa Musa's gold reportedly destabilized Mediterranean gold prices; enabled spread of Islam to West Africa

name: Amber Road
description: Ancient trade route connecting Baltic amber sources to Mediterranean markets, also carrying tin and other northern goods southward
economic_impact: Established one of Europe's earliest long-distance trade corridors; amber found in Egyptian and Mycenaean tombs proves antiquity of network

name: Incense Route
description: Overland route carrying frankincense and myrrh from southern Arabia through the Nabataean kingdom to Mediterranean ports
economic_impact: Generated enormous wealth for Arabian kingdoms; Nabataean city of Petra became one of the ancient world's richest trading cities; frankincense worth its weight in gold

name: Phoenician Mediterranean Network
description: Phoenician maritime trading network spanning the entire Mediterranean from Tyre to the Strait of Gibraltar, establishing colonies and trading posts
economic_impact: Spread the Phoenician alphabet (ancestor of Greek, Latin, and Arabic scripts); Carthage became dominant western Mediterranean power; established template for maritime commercial empires

name: Viking Eastern Trade Route
description: Norse trade route from Scandinavia through Russian rivers to Constantinople and the Caspian, exchanging furs, amber, and slaves for silver and silk
economic_impact: Foundation of Kievan Rus state; brought enormous quantities of Islamic silver to Scandinavia; connected Nordic and Byzantine/Islamic economic spheres

name: Portuguese Cape Route
description: Vasco da Gama's sea route around Africa to India, bypassing overland intermediaries and establishing direct European maritime trade with Asia
economic_impact: Disrupted centuries-old Arab-Indian Ocean trade networks; established Portuguese maritime empire; enabled direct European access to Asian spice markets at fraction of overland cost

name: Arab Indian Ocean Network
description: Arab dhow-based trading network connecting Arabian Peninsula, Persian Gulf, East African coast, and western Indian Ocean
economic_impact: Spread Islam to East Africa; created Swahili language and culture through Arab-Bantu contact; cowrie shells became currency across Africa; established Indian Ocean as interconnected economic zone

name: Malay Archipelago Trade
description: Maritime trade networks throughout the Malay Archipelago connecting India, China, and the Spice Islands via entrepot ports
economic_impact: Malacca became the richest port in Southeast Asia; spread of Hinduism, Buddhism, then Islam to the region; Malay became the lingua franca of maritime Southeast Asia

name: Atlantic Slave Trade Triangle
description: Triangular trade carrying manufactured goods to Africa, enslaved people to the Americas, and sugar/tobacco/cotton back to Europe
economic_impact: Forcibly transported 12+ million Africans; generated enormous wealth for European economies; created plantation economies in Americas; produced creole languages and diaspora cultures

name: European Atlantic Commerce
description: Transatlantic commercial routes connecting Europe with the Americas, carrying silver, sugar, tobacco, and colonial products
economic_impact: Spanish silver from Potosi transformed global economy; Columbian Exchange reshaped agriculture worldwide; created first truly global economic system

name: Hanseatic League Network
description: Northern European merchant confederation controlling Baltic and North Sea trade in furs, amber, fish, grain, and timber
economic_impact: Dominated northern European commerce for centuries; established commercial law precedents; Lubeck became one of Europe's wealthiest cities; proto-capitalist trading organization

name: Indian Ocean Monsoon Route
description: Ancient monsoon-driven trade route connecting Arabia and Persia to India's western coast, leveraging seasonal winds for reliable passage
economic_impact: Hippalus's discovery of monsoon wind patterns revolutionized Indian Ocean trade; enabled regular direct sailing between Arabia and India; carried bulk commodities as well as luxuries

name: Grand Trunk Road
description: One of Asia's oldest and longest trade roads spanning the Indian subcontinent from Kabul to Kolkata, serving as the backbone of South Asian overland trade
economic_impact: Kipling called it "the backbone of all Hind"; facilitated movement of armies, merchants, and pilgrims for over 2000 years; connected Indian Ocean trade to Central Asian networks

name: Tea Horse Road
description: Ancient network of caravan paths through mountainous terrain linking tea-producing regions of Yunnan and Sichuan with Tibet, exchanging tea for Tibetan horses
economic_impact: One of the world's highest and most treacherous trade routes; tea became essential to Tibetan diet and culture; horse-tea exchange shaped Sino-Tibetan relations for centuries

name: Volga Trade Route
description: River-based trade route along the Volga connecting Scandinavia with the Caspian Sea and Islamic world, carrying furs and slaves southward and silver northward
economic_impact: Khazar and Bulgar cities became wealthy trading hubs; enormous hoards of Islamic dirhams found in Scandinavia attest to volume of trade; key conduit between Norse and Islamic worlds

name: Lapis Lazuli Route
description: One of the oldest known long-distance trade routes, carrying lapis lazuli from Afghanistan's Badakhshan mines to Mesopotamia and Egypt
economic_impact: Evidence of this route found in Sumerian royal tombs (3rd millennium BCE); lapis lazuli in Egyptian tombs proves 5000+ years of continuous trade; among the earliest evidence of international commerce

name: Tin Route
description: Maritime route carrying Cornish tin from Britain through the Bay of Biscay and along the Atlantic coast to Mediterranean bronze-producing centers
economic_impact: Tin was essential for bronze production; Cornwall's tin deposits drove long-distance maritime trade centuries before the Roman era; connected Atlantic Europe to Mediterranean civilizations

name: King's Highway
description: Ancient highway running from Egypt through the Levant to Mesopotamia, one of the oldest continuously used trade roads in the world
economic_impact: Referenced in the Hebrew Bible; vital artery connecting Egyptian, Levantine, and Mesopotamian economies; intersected with the Incense Route at Petra

name: Dutch VOC Spice Network
description: Dutch East India Company's global maritime network monopolizing spice trade from Southeast Asia to European markets via the Cape of Good Hope
economic_impact: VOC was world's first multinational corporation; peak market cap equivalent to $7.9 trillion; monopolized nutmeg and clove trade through military force; established colonial control across Southeast Asia

name: Salt Road (Via Salaria)
description: Roman road from Rome to the Adriatic coast, originally built for transporting salt (sal) from coastal salt pans to inland settlements
economic_impact: Roman soldiers were partially paid in salt (origin of "salary"); salt was essential for food preservation; Via Salaria was one of Rome's earliest roads and economic lifelines

name: Canton Trade System
description: Restricted Chinese trade system channeling all Western maritime commerce through the single port of Canton (Guangzhou)
economic_impact: Generated enormous customs revenue for Qing Dynasty; tea exports created massive British trade deficit leading to opium trade; trade imbalance triggered Opium Wars that reshaped East Asian geopolitics

name: Fur Trade Route (North America)
description: River-based fur trade network across northern North America, using canoe routes through the Great Lakes and rivers to connect indigenous trappers with European markets
economic_impact: Drove European exploration and colonization of interior North America; created Metis culture; beaver pelts shaped European fashion; Hudson's Bay Company governed vast territories; indigenous peoples became integrated into global economy

name: Jade Road
description: Trade route carrying jade from Myanmar (Burma) mines to China, where jade was valued above gold as the "stone of heaven"
economic_impact: Jade was the most valued material in Chinese civilization; Myanmar's jadeite deposits were world's primary source; trade shaped Sino-Burmese diplomatic relations for millennia
